_meta.note: Captured off the wire: one real `opencode acp` 1.18.30 turn whose ONLY tool is a Crew MCP directive tool. The MCP server rode the `session/new` `mcpServers` array as a stdio element named `kirocrew-core` exposing `monitor_start`; the model was a local OpenAI-compatible stub with no credential and no network, and it was driven to call that tool once. A SLICE of the turn -- the agent_message_chunk frames and the harness's repeated retries of the same call are omitted, and the three frames kept are verbatim. What this fixture is evidence FOR: opencode names an MCP tool `<server>_<tool>` with ONE underscore and emits no `_meta.kiro` anywhere, so `title` is the only channel naming the tool; `rawInput` is `{}` on the `tool_call` and complete on the following `in_progress` update; and the tool's own result text, directive marker included, arrives verbatim in `content[].content.text` and again in `rawOutput.output`. The marker itself grants nothing -- the directive is claimed out of band from the call's own rawInput (`dashboard/directive_queue`), never from this text. Before the fix, that title resolved to no directive tool at all and every #755 tool answered while applying nothing.
